articles.title: Design Patterns of Agentic AI
articles.excerpt: The Design Patterns Nobody Told You About Agentic AI Here's a confession: the first "agent" I built was basically a while loop with a prompt stapled to it. It called a function, read the result, and c…
articles.body: The Design Patterns Nobody Told You About Agentic AI Here's a confession: the first "agent" I built was basically a while loop with a prompt stapled to it. It called a function, read the result, and called another function. I thought I'd invented something. Turns out I'd just rediscovered ReAct, badly, three years after everyone else. That's the funny thing about agentic AI right now. Underneath all the hype and the funding rounds and the "autonomous agent" landing pages, there are maybe seven recurring patterns doing all the real work. Once you can name them, you start seeing them everywhere: in LangChain's docs, in Claude Code's architecture, in that one open-source repo you starred and never opened again. Let's name them properly. 1.

articles.body: If your AI assistant keeps giving generic, unreliable answers, the problem is not the model. It is the missing structure around it. That is exactly what Agent Skills solve. Modern LLMs are strong enough to handle complex tasks. The real issue is that they are working without stable context, rules, or domain-specific instructions that guide how they should behave in your environment. This is where Agent Skills change the equation. Table of Contents Agent Skills Overview Why Agent Skills? How Do Agent Skills Work?

articles.excerpt: When Capability Becomes Consequential On August 18, 2026, OpenAI disclosed that it had temporarily slowed frontier model development. The immediate reasons were unusually concrete. An earlier cybersec…
articles.body: When Capability Becomes Consequential On August 18, 2026, OpenAI disclosed that it had temporarily slowed frontier model development. The immediate reasons were unusually concrete. An earlier cybersecurity evaluation resulted in OpenAI models identifying and chaining vulnerabilities across OpenAI's research environment and Hugging Face's production infrastructure. Separately, preliminary evaluations of an upcoming model called Astra produced results strong enough that OpenAI says it cannot rule out its Critical cybersecurity capability threshold. OpenAI subsequently paused reinforcement-learning training on its latest deployable models for two weeks. Its largest planned frontier reinforcement-learning run remains on hold.

articles.title: How I Found an SSR Cache Isolation Failure in a React Data Fetching Library
articles.excerpt: There's a certain kind of bug that only shows up when you stop thinking about what code does and start thinking about when it does it. Most security researchers spend their time asking "can an attacke…
articles.body: There's a certain kind of bug that only shows up when you stop thinking about what code does and start thinking about when it does it. Most security researchers spend their time asking "can an attacker make this code do something bad?" That's a fine question. But it misses an entire category of vulnerabilities that have nothing to do with malicious input. Sometimes the code does something bad all on its own, just because of how it's structured. This is the story of one of those bugs. The Setup I was auditing a popular React data fetching library. You've probably used it or at least seen it in a Next.js project. It's the kind of library that handles caching, revalidation, and all the other unglamorous parts of making API calls from React components.

articles.body: The entire pitch of The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild was freedom. It offered a then-unexpected fully open world, the ability to tackle quests in any order, ignore most of the side content, and solve problems in any wacky way that occurred to you. This is one of the reasons why playing Breath of the Wild for the very first time is an experience that so many of us ache to recreate. I’m so, so, so sorry to confirm that despite all of my research, we still cannot deliver that precise feeling — but playing the game with one of these replay strategies in mind can make Hyrule feel new again (and give you a new excuse to be a menace in that beautiful, oh-so-breakable open world). articles.body: On Episode 225 of This Week In Space , Rod Pyle and Tariq Malik are joined by Adam Kall of KMI to discuss their work on the ISS, the goals of the company, and how nature — via the humble octopus and gecko lizards — may provide answers for orbital debris mitigation. The mitigation of orbital debris is an increasingly serious problem that has not gotten enough attention, but this is changing. Commercial companies are addressing orbital debris, and one of them, KMI Space, has flown its experiments aboard the International Space Station, performing over 170 individual rendezvous-and-grab operations. The results are very promising, and the company is moving ahead with ever more ambitious designs. Download or subscribe to this show at: https://twit.tv/shows/this-week-in-space .

articles.title: When is the next lunar eclipse?
articles.excerpt: When will Earth's shadow cover the moon next following the August 2026 partial lunar eclipse?
articles.body: August's "almost Blood Moon" partial lunar eclipse has come and gone, delighting stargazers with a gorgeous natural light show as light filtered by our planet's atmosphere turned it a deep crimson around the point of maximum eclipse. But when is the next lunar eclipse ? Earth won't darken the moon again until Feb. 20, 2027, when a penumbral eclipse will cast our planet's soft outer shadow across February's full "Snow Moon" , so named for the freezing weather that occurs around the time it rises. articles.title: On this day in space! Aug. 29, 1965: NASA's Gemini 5 breaks spaceflight duration record after 2 astronauts spent '8 days in a garbage can'
articles.excerpt: On Aug. 29, 1965, two NASA astronauts returned to Earth after spending eight days in space on the record-setting Gemini 5 mission, setting the stage for longer trips to the moon.
articles.body: On Aug. 29, 1965, two NASA astronauts returned from their record-breaking Gemini 5 mission . Astronauts Gordon Cooper and Pete Conrad spent eight days in Earth orbit, and for the first time, the United States set a world record for the duration of a crewed spaceflight. The Gemini 5 mission launched on Aug. 21, 1965 atop a Titan II rocket from what was then the Cape Canaveral Air Force Station (now the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station ) in Florida. While in orbit, the astronauts were supposed to test rendezvous capabilities and maneuvers using a pod that deployed from their spacecraft. But due to an electrical problem, they had to cancel those plans along with several science experiments.

articles.title: Meeting Nancy Grace Roman: What was the 'mother of Hubble' really like?
articles.excerpt: Nearly a decade ago, I found myself laughing alongside Nancy Grace Roman: one of the most iconic women in astronomy.
articles.body: Nearly a decade ago, I found myself laughing alongside one of the most iconic women in astronomy. This week, a telescope bearing her name launches to the stars . So let's travel back in time and meet Nancy Grace Roman together. Standing under a tent in Washington D.C. at the 2017 inaugural "March for Science," a hodgepodge of scientists and reporters crowd together as the rain pours down outside. "That's Nancy Roman," I hear Bill Nye whisper to me as we stood on the outskirts of the tent. And as I struggled to keep my cool next to one of my childhood heroes, here he is pointing out another. Looking across the room, I see her. There, in the corner of the tent, a woman with white hair wearing a "science not silence" pin sits by herself, soaking in the scenery.

articles.title: ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude quietly get worse over time. This hidden setting fixes them
articles.excerpt: Your favorite AI chatbot might be remembering a little too much.
articles.body: I’ve been using LLM-based AI in some capacity for roughly half a decade, and in that time, the industry has changed significantly. Not only have newer competitors like Gemini and Claude arrived on the scene, but older tools like ChatGPT have also evolved dramatically. We’ve seen better third-party app integration, increased reasoning capabilities, and countless other advancements. However, I would argue that the ability to retain memories matters most. Retaining context from previous conversations helps the AI better anticipate your needs within a single session. It also allows the tool to learn more about you, ensuring that future conversations are tailored to your preferences. However, there is a real downside to memory accumulation that not everyone considers.
